title: Hardware–software co-design
outline: Lecture 16 video (Data Science, COM3021): 'Hardware–software co-design' (title card 'Co-design'). 11 scenes, 132 s. Script: videos/_plan/ds-16-script.md. Running example Leafly (lesson ds-l16-01.js STAGES / COPY / plan(): 132, 40, 32.5, 79 ms). COLOURS: blue CPU and software; purple GPU and hardware; green specialised chip and wins; orange data on the move and demand; red problems; grey frames and labels. titleCard.title: Co-design
titleCard.sub: Hardware and software, made for each other

title: One chip can't do it all
for every job
caps: Leafly: snap a leaf, get the plant's name.
Today the photo goes to the cloud. Answer: a few seconds.
AI pushes general hardware to its limits.
Moore's law is slowing: waiting won't do it.
A new chip is very expensive, so it needs large demand.

title: Hardware and software,
made for each other
caps: Hardware designed around the software it will run.
Software tuned to make full use of that hardware.
Both shaped by each other: hardware–software co-design.

title: Full grids, empty grids,
and the move to the edge
caps: AI models run on tensor operations.
Images: dense tensors. Recommendations: sparse ones.
AI usually runs in the cloud.
Personal models move it onto the phone: edge computing.

title: New chips in cars
and data centres
caps: Cars: ADAS chips see the road and brake in milliseconds.
Data centres: DPUs and IPUs sit beside the CPU.
They take networking, storage and security off its hands.

title: Chip first, code first,
or both at once
caps: Bottom-up: hardware first, software later. Early GPU computing.
Top-down: the workload drives the chip. Volta tensor cores.
Co-design: both together. Snapdragon Ride Flex and Ride Vision.
Demand, software, hardware, round again: an iterative loop.

title: Fast and fixed,
or flexible and slower
caps: Six Leafly jobs. Which go into hardware?
Heavy, stable jobs to hardware: speed and parallelism.
Rules that change stay in software, easy to update.
Simulate chip and code together before building anything.
High-level synthesis: describe the behaviour, get an HDL design.

title: Profile first,
then watch the copies
caps: One photo on the phone's CPU: 132 ms.
The network takes 120 of them.
Network on the GPU: 40 ms, but 13 ms of it is copying.
A GPU twice as fast: only 32.5 ms.
A photo 4 times as big: copies take 52 ms.

title: Match the work to the chip,
let the stack translate
caps: CPU: varied tasks. GPU: maths in parallel. Specialised: stable work.
CPU prepares, GPU runs the network, CPU shows the answer.
Framework, compiler, runtime: the stack maps the model to the chip.

title: Measure the whole pipeline,
then go round again
caps: Measure latency, throughput, energy per result and cost.
Prototype, measure end to end, revisit the partition.
Speed one part up and the bottleneck moves.
Co-design trades power, performance, cost and time.

points.head:
Co-design: hardware and
software, shaped for
each other

Partition: heavy, stable jobs
in hardware, changing ones
in software

Profile, count the copies,
measure the whole pipeline
